# Independent audit: full-space affine negative-power buffer

Audited source: `candidate 5a3c8a5af6aaf266`, Sections 1–7. Verdict: PASS, analytically. The original bad-body compactness/minor theorems and the expressly conditional regular-singleton continuation remain dependencies. No correction found.

## 1. Relative geometry and parameter normalization

The mixed centroid is in the relative interior of the canonical hull: a nonnegative supporting affine function of zero mean must vanish almost everywhere on every positive full-dimensional sampled fiber. Its continuous coefficient vanishes; its remaining affine base restriction vanishes on all sampled bases, hence on the entire relative span. This contradicts a nonzero relative supporting functional.

The support-distance formula varies continuously under positive-fiber Hausdorff convergence, as do the mixed centroid and the canonical hull. Compactness therefore gives one positive relative inradius. An affine function of arithmetic mean one has value one at this centroid. Nonnegativity on the inball bounds its relative linear coefficient, and bounded centroids bound its constant coefficient. Directions orthogonal to the relative span are correctly excluded from the parameter space.

The normalization algebra is exact: after setting h=L/<L>, the negative-power constraint gives <L>=<h^(-r)>^(1/r). If a limiting h is uniformly positive on the canonical hull, coefficient convergence and Hausdorff convergence make this formula stable. No centroid-only positivity is substituted for positivity on the entire hull.

## 2. Boundary divergence under joint limits

The cone from a zero of a nonnegative affine h to a positive-height interior section lies in the actual convex fiber. Its section area is a positive constant times s^(d-1), and coarea supplies the factor 1/||c||. The integral s^(d-1-r) diverges exactly for r>=d. The d=1 convention uses H_0 mass one; r=d gives a logarithmic divergence.

Under joint body/affine convergence, every fixed interior point of the positive limiting fiber eventually belongs to the approximating bodies, and their indicators converge almost everywhere. Fatou on the nonnegative inverse-power integrands therefore preserves the divergence, even though the limiting zero itself may not belong to any approximating body. A limiting fiber on which h vanishes identically gives pointwise infinite limits on its interior and is also covered.

The simplex example for r<d has projection density d t^(d-1) and finite inverse moment d/(d-r), so the claimed sharpness of this compactness mechanism is correctly scoped.

## 3. Escape and attained bad sublevels

If h has a zero anywhere in the canonical convex hull, affinity and nonnegativity force a zero on at least one actual sampled fiber. Hence the normalization scale tends to infinity. If its continuous coefficient is nonzero, h has strictly positive average on EVERY positive fiber, so every actual centroid multiplier diverges. If that coefficient vanishes, the zero set is a nonempty proper exposed base face, and divergence occurs at every sampled base outside it. These alternatives exhaust the possible coefficient limits because the mixed mean of h is one.

The appropriate arithmetic theorem then chooses a fixed limiting base of atomic depth at least M/k: the ordinary occupied-parity theorem in the first case, the complement-face quota theorem in the second. Positive centroid energy, a uniform covariance lower bound and the diverging multiplier force every buffered cap to capture all nonnegative-base-drift fibers. Pure-base caps give equality with atomic depth. Finite atomic trace sets make the selected depth continuous in the changing weights, contradicting the strict bad sublevel.

Positive finite parameter limits give all-direction buffered-depth continuity via the existing uniform slab estimate. The source thus proves fixed-epsilon attainment over the full stated affine parameter class. Its constant-parameter comparison gives convergence of minimum values only. No bound uniform as epsilon tends to zero or automatic properness conclusion is asserted.

## 4. Changed alignment and the conditional source moment

The continuous gradient is exactly grad log f=a_E+c/(N L). The additional term is indispensable; neither the old aligned normal balance nor a projective-energy boundary response may be imported unchanged.

The added chart identity also checks: its right side is (d/N)[1+(N/d)a_E·(x-y)]+L(x)/(N L(y)). The first bracket is nonnegative by the energy-root supporting plane, while the second term is strictly positive. Thus the changed chart is positive on the whole fiber, without becoming an optimal energy chart or acquiring a centroidality property.

At a fixed body, differentiating the normalizing factor <(L+t phi)^(-r)>^(1/r) gives -<L^(-r-1)phi>. Hence dot L=phi-L A_phi and dot f/f=(phi/L-A_phi)/N, with the source's signs and powers. Strict positivity on compact C permits both signs of every full-space affine phi.

Under the separately stated regular-singleton covering interface, the raw quantile response is consequently delta_i(phi(Y_i)/L(Y_i)-A_phi)/N. A finite separator and two-sided affine directions yield the displayed moment identity. Testing constants first and then coordinates produces precisely the L^(-r-1)-tilted FULL mixed mean in the convex hull of the selected marks. The target measure is not the original uniform mixed measure. This is a conditional response consequence, not an assertion that arbitrary atomic/supporting/multiple-contact menus already satisfy that linear interface.

The new parameter class therefore has a rigorous attained setting and genuinely new allowed affine directions. The physical response and payment questions with its changed continuous gradient remain separate.
